title: Wesley's journal
hookLine: 24 May 1738: someone reading Luther's preface to Romans, and a warmed heart
tomorrow: who would ever ask God to put them to suffering?

cards: Before-and-after posts. The day I quit. The day everything changed.
People love a story with a timestamp. Christians have one too, and they argue, kindly, about what it means.
John Wesley, an Anglican priest who would go on to start the Methodist movement, went to a meeting he didn't want to attend. And his journal records exactly what happened at a quarter to nine.

teach.b: Here's the entry for May 24, 1738. "In the evening I went very unwillingly to a society in Aldersgate Street." Someone there was reading Martin Luther's preface to Paul's letter to the Romans.
About a quarter before nine, while the reader described the change God works in the heart through faith in Christ, Wesley writes: "I felt my heart strangely warmed."
He says he trusted Christ alone, and was given assurance his sins were taken away, "even mine." Now the two views. One side says: this is what faith looks like.

A night you can name, a heart you can feel, a date in the diary. Some Methodists and evangelical Christians tell their own stories with a moment like this, and it gives them something to come back to.

teach.h: OR A LONG ROAD OF SUNDAYS.
teach.b: The other side says: faith is mostly a long road, begun in baptism, grown in a church, in years of ordinary Sundays. And they can point to Wesley too. He had been a priest for years before that night.
And in the same entry, he admits that doubts came back almost at once, and he prayed through them.
So the warmed heart didn't end the road. Both sides can hold his journal and say: see?

how: Some Methodists remember Aldersgate Day on May 24; across churches, some Christians tell their faith as a moment they can date, and others as growth from baptism and years in a congregation.

games.q: your faith came slowly, over years. a friend says hers began on one night she can name. she asks you for the best case for her side. what do you say?
o: a dated moment gives you something to come back to when doubt hits, like Wesley's diary.
a moment proves her faith is stronger than people who grew slowly.
if you can't name the night, your faith didn't really start.
games.why: the best case for the moment is the journal itself: a date and an hour to return to. the best case for the long road is in it too: years of priesthood before, and doubt right after.

practice: Read one line of Romans out loud, slowly, the letter Wesley was hearing about that night: "For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death."
Read it a second time as if you'd never heard it. Then sit, and let whatever it stirs, or doesn't, be enough.
